zones: exile and other explicitly authorized cast zones
objects: card or copy proposed as a spell
objects selected as targets or costs
state_reads: available mana sources and restricted mana
state_writes: spell stack item and frozen choices
costs: convoke, improvise, and affinity where compiled
selected life, discard, sacrifice, exile, and tap costs
timing: requires priority except for an internal rules instruction
ordinary noninstant spells require sorcery timing
instant and represented flash permissions use instant timing
mana abilities run after the cost option is determined and before mana is paid
state-based actions and cast triggers stabilize before priority
targets: represented target schemas are selected and validated before payment
target snapshots are stored on the spell
choices: represented face, cost option, X, modes, targets, cost objects, and mana plan
hidden_information: other-zone casts require a compiled permission
face-down exile look permission is not generic
apnap: opponent-made casting choices and controller-first exceptions are not represented
layers: selected effective type and keyword information is consulted
prospective characteristics after moving to the stack are not evaluated generically
replacement_effects: cost and zone-change replacement ordering is not complete
copy: casting a copy and complete copy characteristic handling are not generic
control_change: the spell stack item is controlled by its caster
zone_change: the supported implementation currently moves the object to the stack after choices and payments rather than at CR 601.2a's first announcement step
failed submitted commands restore the authoritative transaction snapshot
source_leaves: objects paid as costs can leave before cast triggers are dispatched

implementation.component: CommanderEngine priority advertisement, _cast, cost-option, target-validation, mana-payment, transaction, stack, and cast-trigger paths

known_blockers: the spell object is moved to the stack after choices and costs instead of before CR 601.2b-h, so prospective stack characteristics and cost effects can be wrong
complete splice, alternative/additional-cost, X, hybrid, Phyrexian, and variable-choice grammar is absent
target-count conditions, must-target effects, target triggers, division, and distribution are incomplete
the complete increase, reduction, minimum, direct-set, and payment-method cost ordering is not generic
not every cost can be paid in every legal order and not every partial-payment interaction is represented
complete prohibition, as-though-flash, conditional-flash, alternative-characteristic, and face-down-exile permission evaluation is absent
later choices cannot generically validate earlier modes, costs, targets, or divisions
opponent-made and simultaneous casting choices lack the CR 601.7 routing model
cost-changing effects do not use a universal prospective-cost model with immutable announced totals
full illegal-action restoration and replay evidence across every casting choice family remains incomplete
